summary:
The starting-pitcher category is the day's biggest red flag across all three ratings — SP is cold and bleeding, with R1 and R2 both sitting at 40% over the last 14 days (76-113, n=189) against a 50% season baseline, a full 10-point collapse, and every rating carrying a live 3-game losing streak on that category. R3's SP is only marginally better at 43% (-7.7pts) but still deep in the same losing trend. Fade SP-driven picks today regardless of which rating fires it — this isn't noise, it's a shared signal across the model.

On the flip side, bullpen is the category to lean into: all three ratings show identical HOT readings at 56% over the last 14 (105-84, n=189), a clean +5.0pt bump over season baseline. Pair that with trends, which is running hot everywhere at 57% (107-82, n=189) and anchors the best category combo in the shop — trends+runs at 55.9% (199-157, n=356) — with trends+bullpen right behind at 55.2% (179-145, n=324). If a pick today has trends and bullpen agreeing, that's your highest-confidence stack. Strong-play units tell a cautionary tale short-term: R1 and R2 are flat-to-negative over the last 7-14 days (R2 -5.0u at 14d, 46-44), while R3 is the only rating showing positive recent strong-play flow (+2.0u over 14d, and +15.0u over 30d at 52%). Season-long, R3 leads the pack at 54% (127-109, +32.0u), followed by R2 (+25.0u) and R1 (+24.0u) — lean R3 when strong-play signals are tight.

On team trust, TBR is the standout when the model likes them — 73% overall (22-8) and a blistering 81% on strong plays (17-4, +20.0u). BOS (76%, 25-8) and DET (67%, +14.0u strong) are also money teams to ride. Avoid HOU strong plays entirely — 22% (2-7, -8.0u) is a glaring bleed despite a respectable 58% overall mark, meaning the model's conviction reads are backwards on Houston right now.
